---
title: "Survey Research Report"
date: "`r format(Sys.Date(), '%B %d, %Y')`"
format:
  html:
    toc: true
    toc-depth: 3
    toc-location: left
    embed-resources: true
    theme: [cosmo, report.scss]
    code-fold: true
    # Equations as MathML: no script, so an offline report shows them (8b-R).
    html-math-method: mathml
    grid:
      sidebar-width: 280px
      body-width: 900px
      margin-width: 160px
  docx:
    reference-doc: apa-reference.docx
    toc: true
  odt:
    reference-doc: apa-reference.odt
    toc: true
  pdf:
    toc: true
    # Tables single-spaced in a smaller size, as APA 7 allows, so that 10
    # columns fit the text width (Codex P1-05).
    include-in-header:
      text: |
        \usepackage{etoolbox}
        \AtBeginEnvironment{longtable}{\footnotesize\setlength{\tabcolsep}{4pt}\ifdefined\setstretch\setstretch{1}\fi}
        % A new page when less than #1 is left on this one, so a table's
        % number and title stay with it (the needspace package's test,
        % written out so no extra package is needed).
        \newcommand{\sfneedspace}[1]{\par\penalty-100\begingroup\dimen0=#1\relax\dimen2=\pagegoal\advance\dimen2 by -\pagetotal\ifdim\dimen0>\dimen2\vfill\penalty-10000\fi\endgroup}
    fontsize: 12pt
    linestretch: 2
    geometry: margin=1in
  typst:
    toc: true
    fontsize: 12pt
    citeproc: true
params:
  instrument_path:     ""
  data_path:           ""
  include_codebook:    true
  include_quality:     true
  include_reliability: true
  include_analysis:    true
  include_missing:     true
  include_descriptives: true
  include_models:      true
  show_code:           true
  plot_palette:        "web"
  interpretations_path: ""
  declarations_path: ""
  content_path:      ""
  provenance_path:   ""
  source_dir:        ""
  instrument_hash:     ""
  analysis_seed:       ""
  use_citations:       false
  fig_width:           ""
  fig_height:          ""
  fig_dpi:             ""
  fig_format:          ""
  quarto_found:        ""
execute:
  echo:    false
  warning: false
  message: false
---

```{r setup}
#| dev: png
# PNG for this chunk alone, which draws nothing: knitr opens its device
# before the svg() check below can run.
library(surveyframe)
library(knitr)

`%||%` <- function(x, y) if (is.null(x)) y else x

# A report source folder (render_report(format = "qmd")) names itself in
# source_dir. sframe_report_source() then reads its .sframe, responses and
# results record, recomputes every number, checks them against the record
# and hands over the same inputs render_report() passes (NAMING decision
# 6). Nothing from the folder's fields is ever written into this file.
src <- if (nzchar(params$source_dir %||% "")) {
  sframe_report_source(params$source_dir, include_analysis = isTRUE(params$include_analysis),
                       plot_palette = params$plot_palette %||% "web")
}
input <- function(name) if (is.null(src)) params[[name]] else src[[name]] %||% ""

# HTML, or Word, OpenDocument and PDF (8b-R). The HTML report keeps its HTML
# tables, numbered figures and notes. Every other format gets pipe tables,
# which pandoc writes as native tables, and a bold title above each figure.
out_html <- knitr::is_html_output()
# Outside HTML each table and figure is numbered as APA 7 sets it (Codex
# P1-04): "Table 1" in bold on its own line, the title in italics on the
# next, both above the float. Pandoc's own caption would put "Table 1:
# Title" on 1 line, so the 2 lines are written here as paragraphs in Word,
# OpenDocument, Typst and LaTeX alike. `cap` is the caption a chunk gives
# through tbl-cap in HTML. Row names repeat the first column, so they are left out
# in every format. Headings come from the label map both engines use
# (Codex P1-03): words, italic symbols and the confidence level. In HTML the
# headings are HTML, so the cells and any given headings are escaped here.
tbl_n <- 0L
fig_n <- 0L
float_head <- function(kind, n, title) sprintf("\n**%s %d**\n\n*%s*\n\n", kind, n, title)
# A float's number and title stay on the page of their table or figure
# (Session UF, the RF follow-up). They could land at a page foot apart from
# it: Figure 2 in Typst, Table 2 in LaTeX. A figure and its 2 lines go in 1
# block that does not break, a minipage in LaTeX. A table may run over a
# page, so in LaTeX it starts a new page when fewer than 5 lines are left,
# and in Typst its 2 lines stick to it, which needs Typst 0.12 or later
# (block's sticky). An older Typst keeps a table of up to 12 rows whole in 1
# block instead, and a longer one as before.
out_to <- knitr::pandoc_to() %||% ""
typst_sticky <- identical(out_to, "typst") && local({
  bin <- Sys.getenv("QUARTO_BIN_PATH")
  q <- file.path(bin, if (.Platform$OS.type == "windows") "quarto.exe" else "quarto")
  if (!nzchar(bin) || !file.exists(q)) q <- Sys.which("quarto")
  v <- tryCatch(suppressWarnings(system2(q, c("typst", "--version"), stdout = TRUE, stderr = FALSE)),
                error = function(e) character(0))
  v <- regmatches(v, regexpr("[0-9]+\\.[0-9]+(\\.[0-9]+)?", v))
  length(v) > 0 && utils::compareVersion(v[1], "0.12") >= 0
})
raw_out <- function(fmt, code) sprintf("\n\n```{=%s}\n%s\n```\n\n", fmt, code)
# Whether a Typst table goes whole in 1 block that does not break.
typst_whole <- function(kind, rows) kind == "Figure" || (!typst_sticky && rows <= 12L)
keep_open <- function(kind, rows = 0L) {
  if (identical(out_to, "typst")) {
    if (typst_whole(kind, rows)) return(raw_out("typst", "#block(breakable: false, width: 100%)["))
    if (typst_sticky) return(raw_out("typst", "#block(sticky: true, breakable: false)["))
  } else if (identical(out_to, "latex")) {
    # setspace sets a minipage single-spaced, so it takes the page's spacing.
    if (kind == "Figure") return(raw_out("latex", paste0(
      "\\edef\\sfstretch{\\baselinestretch}\\noindent\\begin{minipage}{\\linewidth}",
      "\\ifdefined\\setstretch\\setstretch{\\sfstretch}\\fi")))
    return(raw_out("latex", "\\sfneedspace{5\\baselineskip}"))
  }
  ""
}
# Closes keep_open(): `after_head` is TRUE straight after the 2 lines, where
# a sticky Typst block ends, and FALSE after the float, where the others do.
keep_close <- function(kind, rows = 0L, after_head = FALSE) {
  if (identical(out_to, "typst")) {
    whole <- typst_whole(kind, rows)
    if ((after_head && !whole && typst_sticky) || (!after_head && whole))
      return(raw_out("typst", "]"))
  } else if (identical(out_to, "latex") && kind == "Figure" && !after_head) {
    return(raw_out("latex", "\\end{minipage}\\par"))
  }
  ""
}
html_esc <- function(v) {
  v <- gsub("&", "&amp;", v, fixed = TRUE)
  v <- gsub("<", "&lt;", v, fixed = TRUE)
  gsub(">", "&gt;", v, fixed = TRUE)
}
apa_kable <- function(x, ..., caption = NULL, cap = NULL) {
  # Demonstration data stamps each table title (owner 2026-11-05).
  if (isTRUE(content$demo_data)) {
    if (!is.null(caption)) caption <- paste0(caption, " (demonstration data)")
    if (!is.null(cap)) cap <- paste0(cap, " (demonstration data)")
  }
  args <- list(...)
  if (is.null(args$row.names)) args$row.names <- FALSE
  if (is.data.frame(x) && is.null(args$col.names)) {
    args$col.names <- sframe_apa_col_labels(names(x), if (out_html) "html" else "markdown")
  } else if (out_html && !is.null(args$col.names)) {
    args$col.names <- html_esc(args$col.names)
  }
  if (out_html) {
    if (is.data.frame(x)) x[] <- lapply(x, function(v) {
      v <- as.character(v)
      ifelse(is.na(v), NA_character_, html_esc(v))
    })
    return(do.call(kable, c(list(x, format = "html", caption = caption,
                                 escape = FALSE), args)))
  }
  caption <- caption %||% cap
  out <- do.call(kable, c(list(x, format = "pipe"), args))
  if (is.data.frame(x)) out <- pipe_widths(out, x, args$col.names)
  if (is.null(caption)) return(out)
  tbl_n <<- tbl_n + 1L
  rows <- if (is.data.frame(x) || is.matrix(x)) nrow(x) else 0L
  structure(c(keep_open("Table", rows), float_head("Table", tbl_n, caption),
              keep_close("Table", rows, after_head = TRUE), out,
              keep_close("Table", rows)), format = "pipe",
            class = "knitr_kable")
}
# Column widths outside HTML (Codex P1-05). Pandoc sizes the columns of a
# wide pipe table by the dashes under each heading, which kable sets to the
# longest cell, so a column of short identifiers such as sessions_attended
# came out narrower than the identifier and ran into the next column in
# Typst and LaTeX. Each column now gets at least its longest word, and a
# column of long text, which wraps, about 16 characters.
pipe_widths <- function(out, x, heads) {
  plain <- function(v) ifelse(is.na(v), "", gsub("[*~]", "", as.character(v)))
  m <- rbind(plain(heads), as.matrix(data.frame(lapply(x, plain), check.names = FALSE)))
  word <- apply(m, 2, function(col) max(c(1L, nchar(unlist(strsplit(col, "\\s+"))))))
  full <- apply(m, 2, function(col) max(c(1L, nchar(col))))
  width <- pmax(word + 3L, pmin(full, 16L) + 2L)
  at <- grep("^\\|[-:| ]+\\|$", out)[1]
  if (is.na(at)) return(out)
  tok <- strsplit(sub("^\\|(.*)\\|$", "\\1", out[at]), "|", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]
  if (length(tok) != length(width)) return(out)
  left <- startsWith(trimws(tok), ":")
  right <- endsWith(trimws(tok), ":")
  out[at] <- paste0("|", paste0(ifelse(left, ":", ""), strrep("-", pmax(3L, width - left - right)),
                                ifelse(right, ":", ""), collapse = "|"), "|")
  out
}
# A table note, as APA 7 sets it: "Note." in italics, below the table.
apa_note <- function(text) {
  if (is.null(text) || !nzchar(text)) return(invisible())
  if (out_html) cat(sprintf("\n<p class=\"tbl-note\"><em>Note.</em> %s</p>\n\n", text))
  else cat(sprintf("\n*Note.* %s\n\n", text))
}
figure_start <- function(html, title) {
  # The HTML opening is built in R, stamped there. The other formats stamp
  # the title here.
  if (isTRUE(content$demo_data)) title <- paste0(title, " (demonstration data)")
  if (out_html) cat("\n", html, "\n\n", sep = "")
  else {
    fig_n <<- fig_n + 1L
    cat(keep_open("Figure"), float_head("Figure", fig_n, title), sep = "")
  }
}
figure_end <- function() if (out_html) cat("\n\n</figure>\n\n") else cat("\n\n", keep_close("Figure"), sep = "")

# Figure size, resolution and format from render_report(figures = ) (Ethos
# request 19). Empty keeps the defaults. A stated dpi is the pixel density
# the figure is written at, so retina doubling is turned off.
fig_opts <- list()
if (nzchar(params$fig_width %||% ""))  fig_opts$fig.width  <- as.numeric(params$fig_width)
if (nzchar(params$fig_height %||% "")) fig_opts$fig.height <- as.numeric(params$fig_height)
if (nzchar(params$fig_dpi %||% "")) {
  fig_opts$dpi <- as.numeric(params$fig_dpi)
  fig_opts$fig.retina <- 1
}
# svglite writes SVG anywhere. R's own svg() needs Cairo, which on a Mac
# comes with XQuartz: without it capabilities("cairo") still says TRUE, but
# svg() opens nothing and no figure is written. Typst draws SVG by default.
# So where SVG is due and svg() opens no device, svglite draws the figures,
# else PNG.
svg_opens <- function() {
  before <- grDevices::dev.list()
  current <- grDevices::dev.cur()
  f <- tempfile(fileext = ".svg")
  ok <- tryCatch(suppressWarnings({
    grDevices::svg(f)
    opened <- setdiff(grDevices::dev.list(), before)
    if (length(opened)) grDevices::dev.off(opened[[1]])
    length(opened) > 0
  }), error = function(e) FALSE)
  if (current > 1) grDevices::dev.set(current)
  unlink(f)
  isTRUE(ok)
}
svg_due <- identical(params$fig_format %||% "", "svg") ||
  identical(knitr::pandoc_to(), "typst")
if (svg_due) {
  if (identical(params$fig_format %||% "", "svg") && requireNamespace("svglite", quietly = TRUE)) {
    fig_opts$dev <- "svglite"
  } else if (!svg_opens()) {
    if (requireNamespace("svglite", quietly = TRUE)) {
      fig_opts$dev <- "svglite"
    } else {
      fig_opts$dev <- "png"
      fig_opts$fig.ext <- "png"
    }
  }
}
if (length(fig_opts)) do.call(knitr::opts_chunk$set, fig_opts)

instrument <- readRDS(input("instrument_path"))
has_data   <- nzchar(input("data_path")) && file.exists(input("data_path"))
responses  <- if (has_data) readRDS(input("data_path")) else NULL
# Written interpretations keyed by analysis-plan block id, supplied by
# render_report(interpretations = ...). Empty when none were given.
interps    <- if (nzchar(input("interpretations_path")) &&
                  file.exists(input("interpretations_path"))) {
  readRDS(input("interpretations_path"))
} else {
  list()
}
# The codebook table, the distribution charts and the plan results,
# computed by render_report() inside the package (naming decision 6). The
# template prints them, so it and the built-in engine report the same.
content_path <- if (is.null(src)) params$content_path else src$content_path
content <- if (nzchar(content_path %||% "") && file.exists(content_path)) {
  readRDS(content_path)
} else {
  list(codebook_items = NULL, charts = list(), results = NULL)
}

# References (0.4.3). render_report() hands pandoc a CSL-JSON bibliography
# and sets use_citations, so a citation is written in text as [@key] and the
# reference appears once, in the References section at the end. Each result
# used to carry its own reference list, repeating the same works.
use_citations <- isTRUE(as.logical(params$use_citations %||% FALSE))
show_code <- isTRUE(params$show_code %||% TRUE)
cited_keys <- function(target) {
  # A reference linked to nothing counts as cited by the instrument as a
  # whole, so every reference the instrument carries reaches the list.
  refs <- Filter(function(r) target %in% (r$cited_by %||% character(0)) ||
                   (identical(target, "instrument") && !length(r$cited_by)),
                 instrument$references %||% list())
  vapply(refs, function(r) as.character(r$id), character(1))
}
cite <- function(keys) {
  keys <- unique(keys[nzchar(keys)])
  if (!length(keys)) return("")
  paste0("[", paste0("@", keys, collapse = "; "), "]")
}
# Without a bibliography (a host calling the template directly), the method
# references are still gathered here and listed once at the end as text.
fallback_refs <- character(0)
```

<style>
/* Brand look shared with render_results() and the static survey: system font,
   navy headings, teal accent. */
body { font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, "Segoe UI", Roboto, sans-serif;
       color: #1a1a2e; }
h1, h2, h3, h4, h5, #title-block-header .title { color: #1a1a2e; }
a { color: #16B3B1; }
#TOC .active, .sidebar-item .active { color: #16B3B1; }

/* Academic (APA) tables: horizontal rules only, no shading, no vertical lines.
   Each table is its own horizontal-scroll container so wide tables stay within
   the content column. Overrides the theme's default table styling. */
table { display: block; overflow-x: auto; max-width: 100%;
        border-collapse: collapse; margin: 14px 0; }
th, td { padding: 7px 14px; vertical-align: top;
         border: none !important; background: none !important; }
thead th { border-top: 2px solid #1a1a2e !important;
           border-bottom: 1px solid #1a1a2e !important; font-weight: 700; }
tbody tr { background: none !important; }
tbody tr:last-child td { border-bottom: 2px solid #1a1a2e !important; }
.cell-output-display, .cell-output { overflow-x: auto; max-width: 100%; }
/* APA 7 table and figure titles above the float: the number in bold, the
   title in italics below it (CX-22). The theme puts captions below, in grey. */
caption.sf-apa-caption, figcaption.sf-apa-caption {
  caption-side: top; text-align: left; color: inherit;
  font-size: .95em; margin-bottom: 4px; }
figure.sf-figure { margin: 16px 0; }

/* Shared footer */
.sf-foot { text-align: center; font-size: 12px; color: #94a3b8;
           margin-top: 48px; padding-top: 16px; border-top: 1px solid #eee; }
.sf-foot a { color: #16B3B1; font-weight: 600; text-decoration: none; }
/* References, one list at the end in a standard bibliography layout: a
   hanging indent, and a little space between entries. */
#refs .csl-entry, .sf-references p { padding-left: 2em; text-indent: -2em; margin: 0 0 0.6em; line-height: 1.5; }
</style>

```{r meta}
#| output: asis
m <- instrument$meta
cat(sprintf("**Instrument:** %s\n\n", m$title %||% "Untitled"))
cat(sprintf("**Version:** %s\n\n", m$version %||% ""))
if (!is.null(m$description) && nzchar(m$description))
  cat(sprintf("**Description:** %s\n\n", m$description))
if (!is.null(m$authors) && length(m$authors) > 0)
  cat(sprintf("**Authors:** %s\n\n", paste(m$authors, collapse = ", ")))
if (use_citations && length(cited_keys("instrument")) > 0)
  cat(sprintf("**Draws on:** %s\n\n", cite(cited_keys("instrument"))))
cat(sprintf("**Validation status:** %s\n\n",
  if (isTRUE(m$validated)) "Valid" else "Not validated"))
```

## Provenance {#sec-provenance .unnumbered}

```{r provenance}
#| output: asis
# What the report was built from: the instrument hash and its check, the
# amendment count, the responses sha256 and the results record sha256, from
# the table render_report() builds for both engines (NAMING decision 6).
prov <- if (nzchar(input("provenance_path")) && file.exists(input("provenance_path")))
  readRDS(input("provenance_path")) else NULL
if (is.null(prov)) {
  cat("No provenance was recorded for this render.\n\n")
} else {
  print(apa_kable(prov, align = c("l", "l"), caption = "Provenance"))
}
```

```{r codebook-sources, eval=params$include_codebook && use_citations}
#| output: asis
# Where each item and scale comes from, cited in text. The works themselves
# are listed in the References section.
sources <- list()
for (sc in instrument$scales %||% list()) {
  keys <- cited_keys(paste0("scale:", sc$id))
  if (length(keys)) sources[[length(sources) + 1]] <- sprintf("- Scale *%s*: %s", sc$label %||% sc$id, cite(keys))
}
for (it in instrument$items %||% list()) {
  keys <- cited_keys(paste0("item:", it$id))
  if (length(keys)) sources[[length(sources) + 1]] <- sprintf("- Item `%s`: %s", it$id, cite(keys))
}
if (length(sources)) cat("**Sources of items and scales**\n\n", paste(unlist(sources), collapse = "\n"), "\n\n", sep = "")
```

```{r codebook-models, eval=params$include_codebook && !is.null(cb$models_table) && nrow(cb$models_table) > 0}

apa_kable(cb$models_table, cap = "Measurement and structural models",
  col.names = c("ID","Label","Type","Engine","Constructs","Paths"),
  align = c("l","l","l","l","c","c"))
```

## Data Quality {#sec-quality .unnumbered}

```{r quality-check, eval=params$include_quality && has_data}
qr <- sframe_quality_results(responses, instrument)
```

```{r quality-summary, eval=params$include_quality && has_data}
#| output: asis
# The same table and note as the built-in engine (8b-R): the note says why a
# straight-lining chart is absent, computed by render_report().
qs_df <- data.frame(
  Metric = c("Respondents", "Items", "Flagged", "Flag rate"),
  Value = c(qr$summary$n_respondents, qr$summary$n_items, qr$summary$n_flagged,
            sprintf("%.1f%%", qr$summary$flag_rate * 100)),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
print(apa_kable(qs_df, align = c("l", "r"), caption = "Quality summary"))
if (!is.null(content$quality_note))
  cat(if (out_html) sprintf("\n\n<p class=\"sf-note\">%s</p>\n\n", content$quality_note)
      else sprintf("\n\n*%s*\n\n", content$quality_note))
```

```{r quality-attention, eval=params$include_quality && has_data && length(qr$attention) > 0}
#| tbl-cap: !expr if (out_html) "Attention check results"
attn_df <- do.call(rbind, lapply(qr$attention, function(a)
  data.frame(Check=a$check_id, Type=a$type,
    Pass_rate=sprintf("%.1f%%", a$pass_rate*100),
    Failures=a$n_fail, Action=a$fail_action,
    stringsAsFactors=FALSE)))
apa_kable(attn_df, cap = "Attention check results", align=c("l","l","r","r","l"))
```

```{r quality-missing, eval=params$include_quality && has_data}
#| output: asis
miss_pct <- mean(qr$missing$respondent_miss > qr$missing$flagged_threshold, na.rm=TRUE)*100
cat(sprintf("**Respondent missingness:** %.1f%% exceed the %.0f%% threshold.\n\n",
  miss_pct, qr$missing$flagged_threshold*100))
high_miss <- qr$missing$item_miss_rate[qr$missing$item_miss_rate > 0.10]
if (length(high_miss) > 0) {
  print(apa_kable(data.frame(Item=names(high_miss),
    Missing=sprintf("%.1f%%", high_miss*100), stringsAsFactors=FALSE),
    align=c("l","r"), caption = "Items with more than 10% missing"))
} else { cat("No items exceed 10% missing values.\n\n") }
```

```{r quality-sl, eval=params$include_quality && has_data && length(qr$straightline) > 0}

    Flagged=sprintf("%.1f%%", s$flag_rate*100), stringsAsFactors=FALSE)))
apa_kable(sl_df, cap = "Straight-lining by scale", align=c("l","c","r"))

```{r missing-data, eval=params$include_missing && has_data}
#| output: asis
mr <- tryCatch(sframe_missing_data_results(responses, instrument), error = function(e) NULL)
if (is.null(mr)) {
  cat("Missing-data diagnostics could not be computed from the supplied data.\n\n")
} else {
  print(apa_kable(sframe_apa_cells(mr$item_missing), caption = "Item-wise missingness"))
  print(apa_kable(sframe_apa_cells(mr$respondent_missing), caption = "Respondent-wise missingness"))
  patterns_display <- mr$patterns[, intersect(c("description", "n", "percent"), names(mr$patterns)), drop = FALSE]
  print(apa_kable(sframe_apa_cells(patterns_display), caption = "Missing-data patterns"))
  if (!is.null(mr$scale_missing_rules) && nrow(mr$scale_missing_rules) > 0)
    print(apa_kable(sframe_apa_cells(mr$scale_missing_rules), caption = "Scale missing rules"))
}

# Every chart is drawn by render_report() from the shared chart specs, as

if (!is.null(attr(content$charts, "scale_error")))

  if (!is.null(chart$plot)) print(chart$plot) else chart$draw()
  figure_end()

## Reliability {#sec-reliability .unnumbered}

```{r reliability, eval=params$include_reliability && has_data}
#| output: asis
rr <- tryCatch(sframe_reliability_results(responses, instrument), error = function(e) NULL)
if (is.null(rr)) {
  cat("Reliability statistics could not be computed from the supplied data.\n\n")
} else if (length(rr) == 0) {
  cat("No scales with two or more matching response columns found.\n\n")
} else {
  rel_df <- do.call(rbind, lapply(rr, function(s)
    data.frame(Scale=paste0(s$label," (",s$scale_id,")"),
      N_items=s$n_items, N=s$n,
      Alpha   = if (!is.null(s$alpha))   sprintf("%.2f", s$alpha)   else "n/a",
      Omega_h = if (!is.null(s$omega_h)) sprintf("%.2f", s$omega_h) else "n/a",
      Omega_t = if (!is.null(s$omega_t)) sprintf("%.2f", s$omega_t) else "n/a",
      stringsAsFactors=FALSE)))
  print(apa_kable(rel_df,
    col.names=c("Scale","Items","N","Alpha","Omega h","Omega total"),
    align=c("l","c","c","r","r","r"),
    caption="Scale reliability statistics"))
  # The sources of each scale, under its table (8b-R).
  if (use_citations) {
    src_parts <- vapply(rr, function(s) {
      keys <- cited_keys(paste0("scale:", s$scale_id))
      if (length(keys)) paste0(s$label %||% s$scale_id, " ", cite(keys)) else ""
    }, character(1))
    src_parts <- src_parts[nzchar(src_parts)]
    if (length(src_parts)) cat(sprintf("\n*Sources.* %s.\n\n", paste(src_parts, collapse = "; ")))
  }
}
```

## Analysis Plan {#sec-analysis .unnumbered}

```{r study, eval=params$include_analysis && !is.null(content$study)}
#| output: asis
# The study the plan serves (D13 in the report, 8b-R): the problem, its
# sources, and the trace from objectives to research questions, as
# render_report() built it for both engines.
s <- content$study
cat("### Study\n\n")
if (length(s$problem_md) && nzchar(s$problem_md)) {
  if (grepl("\n", s$problem_md, fixed = TRUE)) cat("**Problem:**\n\n", s$problem_md, "\n\n", sep = "")
  else cat("**Problem:** ", s$problem_md, "\n\n", sep = "")
}
if (use_citations && length(cited_keys("study")))
  cat(sprintf("**Sources:** %s\n\n", cite(cited_keys("study"))))
if (!is.null(s$trace))
  print(apa_kable(s$trace, caption = "Objectives and the research questions that serve them"))
if (length(s$unlinked))
  cat(sprintf("\n*Research questions that name no objective: %s.*\n\n", s$unlinked))
```

```{r analysis, eval=params$include_analysis && length(instrument$analysis_plan) > 0}
#| output: asis
# What each block declared before the data prints above its result, and the
# interpretation below it, labelled as written after the results (D12).
# render_report() computes both with the helpers the built-in engine uses,
# so the 2 reports say the same.
decls <- if (nzchar(input("declarations_path")) &&
             file.exists(input("declarations_path"))) {
  readRDS(input("declarations_path"))
} else {
  list(blocks = list())
}
decl_for <- function(b) {
  id <- as.character(b$block_id %||% b$id %||% "")[1]
  if (nzchar(id) && id %in% names(decls$blocks)) decls$blocks[[id]] else list()
}
# The fields as safe Markdown, built in R (8b-R): Markdown, math and
# footnotes kept, shortcodes, raw blocks, fences, headings and HTML printed
# as typed. Printed here as data, so nothing in them is ever run.
declare_md <- function(b) {
  d <- decl_for(b)$declaration_md
  if (length(d) > 0) cat(d, sep = "")
  # The sources of the hypotheses, beside them (8b-R).
  keys <- cited_keys(paste0("hypothesis:", as.character(b$block_id %||% b$id %||% "")[1]))
  if (use_citations && length(keys))
    cat(sprintf("**Sources for the hypotheses:** %s\n\n", cite(keys)))
}
interp_md <- function(b) {
  text <- decl_for(b)$interpretation_md %||% ""
  if (nzchar(text)) cat("\n", text, sep = "")
}
if (!has_data) {
  for (i in seq_along(instrument$analysis_plan)) {
    rq <- instrument$analysis_plan[[i]]
    rq_md <- content$research_questions_md[i] %||% ""
    cat(sprintf("### RQ %d: %s\n\n", i, if (!is.na(rq_md) && nzchar(rq_md)) rq_md else "(untitled)"))
    cat(sprintf("**Planned test:** %s\n\n", rq$test %||% ""))
    if (length(rq$variables %||% character(0)) > 0)
      cat(sprintf("**Variables:** %s\n\n", paste(rq$variables, collapse = ", ")))
    declare_md(rq)
    if (use_citations && length(cited_keys(paste0("plan:", rq$id %||% ""))) > 0)
      cat(sprintf("**Sources:** %s\n\n", cite(cited_keys(paste0("plan:", rq$id %||% "")))))
    interp_md(rq)
  }
} else {
  results <- content$results
  if (!is.list(results)) {
    cat("Analysis plan could not be executed. Check that variable names match response columns.\n\n")
  } else {
    for (i in seq_along(results)) {
      r <- results[[i]]
      cat(sprintf("### RQ %d: %s\n\n", i, if (nzchar(r$research_question_md %||% "")) r$research_question_md else "(untitled)"))
      if (!is.null(r$error)) {
        cat(sprintf("> **Error:** %s\n\n", r$error))
      } else {
        declare_md(r)
        scale_entries <- Filter(function(e) is.list(e) && !is.null(e$scale_id), r)
        # Planned or exploratory, decided by render_report() (owner 2026-11-04).
        if (isTRUE(r$exploratory)) cat(sprintf("**%s**\n\n", r$exploratory_label))
        if (!is.null(r$apa)) {
          cat(sprintf("**Result:** %s\n\n", r$apa))
        } else if (length(scale_entries) == 0) {
          cat("**Result:** see the matching section of this report above.\n\n")
        }
        if (!is.null(r$syntax)) {
          cat("````\n")
          cat(r$syntax)
          cat("\n````\n\n")
        }
        # Only where the result has no table of its own, as the built-in engine
        # shows it, so no 2 tables share a title (CX-22).
        if (is.null(r$apa) && length(scale_entries) > 0 && !is.data.frame(r$table)) {
          rel_tab <- do.call(rbind, lapply(scale_entries, function(s)
            data.frame(
              Scale = paste0(s$label %||% s$scale_id, " (", s$scale_id, ")"),
              Items = s$n_items %||% NA,
              Alpha = if (!is.null(s$alpha)) sprintf("%.2f", s$alpha) else "n/a",
              stringsAsFactors = FALSE)))
          print(apa_kable(rel_tab, align = c("l", "c", "r"), row.names = FALSE,
                      caption = if (out_html) r$caption_html else r$caption_text))
          cat("\n")
        }
        if (!is.null(r$effect_label))
          cat(sprintf("**Effect size:** %s\n\n", r$effect_label))
        if (!is.null(r$table) && is.data.frame(r$table))
          print(apa_kable(sframe_apa_cells(r$table), caption = if (out_html) r$caption_html else r$caption_text))
        # A second table the result carries: the quanteda runner's leading
        # features, or a moderation's conditional slopes at the moderator's own
        # values. Both were retained by their runner and rendered by neither
        # engine. render_report() attaches it with the helper the
        # built-in engine so the 2 agree on what a result shows.
        sup <- r$supplement
        if (!is.null(sup)) {
          cat("\n")
          print(apa_kable(sframe_apa_cells(sup$table),
                      caption = if (out_html) sup$caption_html else sup$caption, row.names = FALSE))
          cat("\n")
        }
        # The statistical call behind the numbers, folded away. Showing this
        # chunk's own code would display the dispatch loop instead, which says
        # nothing about which test ran with which options.
        if (show_code) {
          code <- sframe_syntax_result(r)
          if (!is.null(code)) {
            # Folded in HTML. Elsewhere a fold means nothing, and a callout in
            # Typst makes Quarto import a Typst package from the network, so
            # the code prints as a plain labelled block.
            if (out_html) {
              cat("\n::: {.callout-note collapse=\"true\" title=\"Show R code\"}\n")
            } else {
              cat("\n*R code:*\n\n")
            }
            cat("```r\n", paste(code, collapse = "\n"), "\n```\n", sep = "")
            if (out_html) cat(":::\n\n") else cat("\n")
          }
        }
        # The chart for this result sits directly under its table, as one
        # unit per research question, rather than in a separate section.
        if (!is.null(r$plot)) {
          figure_start(r$figure_open, r$caption_text)
          print(r$plot)
          figure_end()
        }
        interp_md(r)
        # Cited in text. The references themselves are listed once, in the
        # References section at the end.
        block_key <- r$block_id %||% r$id %||% ""
        keys <- c(cited_keys(paste0("plan:", block_key)), names(r$citations %||% list()))
        if (use_citations && length(keys) > 0) {
          cat(sprintf("*References for this analysis:* %s\n\n", cite(keys)))
        } else if (length(r$citations) > 0) {
          fallback_refs <- c(fallback_refs, unlist(r$citations))
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

## Model Appendix {#sec-models .unnumbered}

```{r models, eval=params$include_models && length(instrument$models %||% list()) > 0}
#| output: asis
for (model in instrument$models) {
  cat(sprintf("### %s\n\n", model$label %||% model$id))
  cat(sprintf("**Type:** %s  \n**Engine:** %s\n\n", model$type %||% "", model$engine %||% ""))
  if (use_citations && length(cited_keys(paste0("model:", model$id %||% ""))) > 0)
    cat(sprintf("**Sources:** %s\n\n", cite(cited_keys(paste0("model:", model$id %||% "")))))
  syntax <- tryCatch(
    switch(model$type,
      cfa = sframe_syntax_cfa(instrument = instrument, model = model),
      cb_sem = sframe_syntax_sem(model, instrument = instrument),
      pls_sem = sframe_syntax_pls(model),
      efa = sframe_syntax_efa(unlist(lapply(model$measurement$constructs, function(con) con$items))),
      ""
    ),
    error = function(e) paste("Model syntax could not be generated:", conditionMessage(e))
  )
  cat("```r\n")
  cat(syntax)
  cat("\n```\n\n")
  cat("```json\n")
  cat(sframe_model_json(model, pretty = TRUE))
  cat("\n```\n\n")
}
```

## Reproducibility {#sec-repro .unnumbered}

```{r repro}
#| output: asis
hash_val <- input("instrument_hash")
if (is.null(hash_val) || !nzchar(hash_val)) hash_val <- "see .sframe file"
cat(sprintf("**Instrument version:** %s\n\n", instrument$meta$version %||% ""))
# Outside HTML the 64-character hash takes a line of its own, since it
# cannot break and ran past the LaTeX margin after its label (Codex P1-05).
cat(sprintf("**Instrument hash:**%s`%s`\n\n", if (out_html) " " else "\\\n", hash_val))
# The engine and the seed belong next to the hash: the hash says which
# instrument this describes, the engine says which of surveyframe's 2
# renderers produced it, and the seed says what reproducing the numbers takes.
cat("**Rendering engine:** Quarto\n\n")
# The Quarto copy that rendered it and where it was found: on the PATH, from
# QUARTO_PATH, or bundled with RStudio or Positron.
if (nzchar(params$quarto_found %||% "")) cat(sprintf("**Quarto:** %s\n\n", params$quarto_found))
# Quarto renders in its own R process, so the version and commit name the
# surveyframe that process loaded. RemoteSha is written by remotes and pak.
sf_desc <- utils::packageDescription("surveyframe")
sf_sha <- sf_desc$RemoteSha %||% ""
cat(sprintf("**surveyframe:** %s%s\n\n", sf_desc$Version,
            if (nzchar(sf_sha)) {
              sprintf(", commit `%s`", sub("^([0-9a-f]{12})[0-9a-f]*", "\\1", sf_sha))
            } else ""))
seed_val <- input("analysis_seed")
if (is.null(seed_val) || !nzchar(seed_val)) seed_val <- "not recorded"
cat(sprintf("**Analysis seed:** `%s`\n\n", seed_val))
cat(sprintf("**Report generated:** %s\n\n", format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M %Z")))
# The version a reader holds and how it got there, from the same table the
# built-in engine prints.
if (is.null(content$amendments)) {
  cat("No amendments are recorded.\n\n")
} else {
  cat(sprintf("**Amendments (%d)**, oldest first:\n\n", nrow(content$amendments)))
  cat(paste(apa_kable(content$amendments), collapse = "\n"))
  cat("\n\n")
  # Each deviation report formatted, below the table that keeps it as typed.
  if (length(content$amendment_notes_md)) cat(content$amendment_notes_md, sep = "")
}
cat("**To reproduce:**\n\n")
cat("```r\nlibrary(surveyframe)\n")
cat("instr     <- read_sframe(\"your_instrument.sframe\")\n")
cat("responses <- read_responses(\"your_responses.csv\", instr)\n")
cat("render_report(instr, data = responses, output_file = \"report.html\")\n```\n\n")
```

## References {#sec-references .unnumbered}

```{r references}
#| output: asis
# One list for the whole report, in the bibliography style render_report()
# was given (APA 7 by default), with a hanging indent. pandoc fills the
# refs block with every work cited above, each once.
if (use_citations) {
  cat("::: {#refs .references}\n:::\n\n")
} else if (length(fallback_refs) > 0) {
  refs <- sort(unique(fallback_refs))
  cat("::: {.references .sf-references}\n", paste0(refs, collapse = "\n\n"), "\n:::\n\n", sep = "")
} else {
  cat("No references were cited.\n\n")
}
```
